title: 1997 AHSME Problem 25
statement: Let \(ABCD\) be a parallelogram and let \(\overrightarrow{AA'},\) \(\overrightarrow{BB'},\) \(\overrightarrow{CC'},\) and \(\overrightarrow{DD'}\) be parallel rays in space on the same side of the plane determined by \(ABCD.\) If \(AA'=10,\) \(BB'=8,\) \(CC'=18,\) \(DD'=22,\) and \(M\) and \(N\) are the midpoints of \(A'C'\) and \(B'D',\) respectively, then \(MN=\)

solutions.text: Choose the common ray direction as a unit vector \(u.\) Then \[ \begin{aligned} M&=\frac{A+C}{2}+14u,\\ N&=\frac{B+D}{2}+15u. \end{aligned} \] Since \(A+C=B+D\) for a parallelogram, \(N-M=u,\) so \(MN=1.\) The correct answer is B.
hints: Use vectors and the parallelogram identity \(A+C=B+D\)
The planar components of the two midpoints coincide; compare only their ray-direction components
